title.narrative: Egypt Inclusive Growth For Sustainable Recovery

description.narrative: The development objective of Inclusive Growth for Sustainable Recovery Development Policy Financing Project for Egypt is to: (a) enhance macro-fiscal sustainability; (b) enable private sector development; and (c) foster women's economic inclusion. The operation aims to support more inclusive economic growth for a sustainable recovery at a time of Coronavirus (COVID-19) related turbulence. While this standalone operation focuses on an immediate set of prior actions, the discussions with the government also encompassed proposed medium-term reforms on which there is an active dialogue. The pillars of the operation mainly align with three pillars of the overarching government program, Egypt Takes Off: Economic Development and Improving Government Performance, Job Creation, and Improving Standards of Living, as well as four of the more specific policy areas identified under the NSRP: labor market efficiency, improving the business environment, improving the performance of public institutions through improved governance, and enhancing access to finance. As such, the pillars of the operation are interlinked, and the operation contributes directly to the government's overall vision, its short-term and medium-term objectives to place inclusive growth, job creation, and gender equality at the center of the development agenda, and the achievement of United Nations sustainable development goals (SDGs).

title.narrative: Publication of FRA Board decisions detailing the secondary regulations stipulated by the law

comment.narrative: This RI was fully achieved with a delay. On March 16, 2022, the Financial Regulatory Authority issued Decree No. 58 for 2022 to regulate the licensing process for fintech companies, which is crucial. However, the remaining decrees concerning requirements for equipment, technological infrastructure, information systems, protection and insurance, digital identity, digital contracts, digital registry, compliance requirements, and outsourcing register for financial technology in non-banking financial activities were delayed. Decrees No. 139, 140, and 141 of 2023 were issued in June 2023 and published in the Official Gazette in July 2023.

title.narrative: Cargo inspections at the Port of Alexandria by the Egyptian Customs Authority

comment.narrative: This RI was exceeded. The evidence received on customs total declarations by lane (green and red) highlights that in March 2023, green lane declarations accounted for 21% of the total declarations at Alexandria port, indicating that the target was met. In this context, green signifies no inspection, while red indicates that inspections were conducted.

title.narrative: Amount invested by the private sector in waste management

comment.narrative: The RI was exceeded as it focused on the amount invested rather than executed. On April 4th, 2023, the Ministers of Environment, Electricity and Renewable Energy, Finance, Local Development, and Military Production witnessed the signing of a US$120 million “direct investment” contract for the first municipal waste-to-energy station in Abu Rawash, Giza. This initiative represents a partnership with the private sector. According to sector experts, since the contract was signed in the first week of April, the investments were already in the pipeline by March.

title.narrative: (i) Development and implementation of GBV SOPs for the Code of Conduct based on global best practices and including grievance redress mechanism and evaluation mechanisms for reporting violations

comment.narrative: The RI was fully achieved. Since 2021, Egypt's transportation sector has made significant progress in combating violence against women through collaboration between the National Council for Women and the Ministry of Transport. This includes implementing the Code of Conduct with SOPs, communication strategies, and improved grievance mechanisms. The National Code of Conduct for Transport Users and Workers, issued under Ministerial Resolution No. 237 of 2021, marks a significant step in protecting women from violence and harassment. The strategic cooperation aims to enhance women's safety and empower them in public spaces, with training for Ministry employees and leveraging international best practices. The integration of the Women's Complaints Office into the unified government complaints system and cross-sector collaboration are also key achievements.

title.narrative: Regular publication of annual debt reports and semi-annual debt bulletins

target.value: One annual debt report and one annual debt bulletin

comment.narrative: This RI was partially achieved, primarily due to differing definitions of domestic debt between the Ministry of Finance (MoF) and the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE). However, it is important to note that transparency regarding tradable debt was significantly higher compared to the total debt, which includes the non-tradable component. Similarly, transparency for external debt was higher than that for domestic debt.
